intended_object: The graded deviation D_k : gr_k(G) → gr_{m+k}(G) of a continuous endomorphism θ of a topological group G with θ ≡ id mod λ_m. Here λ_k is the (topologically closed) lower p-series, gr_k = λ_k/λ_{k+1}, and D_k is the additive map induced by g ↦ g⁻¹θ(g), as in Labute's classification of Demushkin groups. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body sends x ∈ λ_k to the class of x⁻¹θ(x) in λ_{m+k}/λ_{m+k+1}. The lemma `inv_mul_apply_mem_pLowerCentralSeries` shows this element lies in λ_{m+k}. `deviationAux` shows the map is a homomorphism, using the crossed-homomorphism identity and the fact that conjugation acts trivially on the graded piece. `subgroupOf_le_ker_deviationAux` shows λ_{k+1} lies in the kernel, so the map factors through gr_k = λ_k/λ_{k+1}, which is the codomain `gradedPiece`. The definition is the `QuotientGroup.lift` of this map, turned into an additive map with `MonoidHom.toAdditive`. So it is the map induced by g ↦ g⁻¹θ(g), as the docstring says.

Indexing starts at λ_0 = G, where Labute starts at λ_1 = G. This is only a shift of convention. The m = 0 case is also handled sensibly (D = θ_* − id).

Generality: G is any topological group and θ any continuous endomorphism. Continuity is needed because the series is defined with topological closures. This is the natural setting for profinite and pro-p groups. Mathlib has no lower p-series and no graded deviation, so there is nothing more general to compare against.
